title: the section name a producer types
claim: Section function is decided from the section's name. The vocabulary was English only, so a Hebrew-named song was planned as neutral sections. B-24 makes one shared vocabulary that speaks Hebrew and stops three writers from hashing the name.

hebrew.reading: The treatment half is closed: identical functions, families, roles, climax layer, task counts and transition devices. Only note counts still move, and their cause is isolated below.

unnamed.reading: Unchanged on purpose. 'Section 3' states nothing and neutral is the honest answer. What it measures is that section function is derived from the name only: no planner can hear form. Recorded, unassigned.

ownerShapeFixture.reading: A Hebrew rename of an eight-section song changes nothing about its treatment; the six differences are all seeded note counts.

controls.positive: renaming the chorus 'Part B' changes its treatment and the check reports it (function_changed) - the comparison has sensitivity
controls.null: the English twin compared with itself shows no drift

changes.what: the only vocabulary: an ordered table per section function, English and Hebrew in one entry, containment traps documented (pre-chorus before chorus, פרה-פזמון before פזמון, breakdown before break)
classifySection delegates to it; decision order unchanged

recognised 'פזמון' in the command and then searched for an English 'chorus' in the project's section names, so a Hebrew instruction about a Hebrew-named song matched nothing; both sides now ask the same vocabulary
the climax name prior reads the vocabulary; MUSICAL_MAP_VERSION 2.2 -> 2.3 so stored maps of Hebrew-named songs are re-derived
which fill is played was hash01(sectionName:bar); now the section's function, occurrence and start bar
timing and velocity jitter were seeded from note.id, and ids carry the section name; now seeded from family, role, onset and pitch

clampPolyphony grouped onsets by whole milliseconds and then compared held notes against the rounded value, so a 30.1 ms overlap read as legal against a 30 ms tolerance; it now judges against the real start of the earliest note in the group

intendedEnglishChanges.name: Pre Chorus
intendedEnglishChanges.why: the old pattern was pre-?chorus, which does not match a space

intendedEnglishChanges.name: Pre Hook
intendedEnglishChanges.why: the old pattern was pre-?hook, which does not match a space

englishParity: every other English name in a 32-name list classifies exactly as the pre-B-24 regexes, which the test keeps verbatim as its reference implementation

goldenFixture.why: only performed timing and velocity moved; the cause is appended to recordedAt in referencePartComposer.golden.test.ts

handoffs.finding: seedFor seeds every part from `part-<sectionName>-<instrument>-<role>` and from musicalMap.inputsDigestSha256, which hashes model.sections with their names. Renaming a section changes the composition seed twice over. One change - identify a part by its position in the form, seed from a digest of the musical content rather than the staleness digest - closes the remaining notes_changed and B-12b defect 7 (duplicate section names -> duplicate note ids).

FAMILY_ALIASES is English only and briefCompiler parses free-text instrumentation, so a Hebrew brief naming פסנתר or כינור would not resolve to a family. Same class of defect, but nobody has measured it: no invariant, no failing run. Recorded rather than fixed on the strength of the analogy.

honestLimits: No human has judged an arrangement because of this stream. It changes which treatment a Hebrew-named song receives, not whether that treatment is good.

The owner's own song is unaffected in its planning: its sections carry English names from the analysis. What did change for it, as for every song, are the performance jitter values and the fill choices.
The unnamed variant stays at 0/20 and keeps its todo. It is a capability gap (inferring section function from the music), not a classifier bug.
The Hebrew vocabulary was chosen deliberately narrow. עלייה was considered and dropped as too common a word to be safe on free text; מעבר reading as an interlude is a judgement, not a measurement.
